summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY. Embedded software engineer writing C/C++ firmware on STM32 (bare-metal and FreeRTOS) and Arduino over UART/I2C/SPI serial protocols, with Python tooling for data acquisition. Debugged a distributed multi-node control system across software, communication and hardware layers: 11 integration failures resolved, 10/10 pick reliability.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth, translating 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python; debugged sensor jitter through software calibration and tuning.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed Python tooling (PyQt, Matplotlib GUI) for real-time data acquisition and visualization in a laboratory; used GitLab for version control and JupyterHub for collaborative analysis and technical documentation.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Guided the coding team on object detection models; authored and taught a Python course for club member onboarding.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built Cortex-M4 temperature monitoring firmware in embedded C at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate within 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM; verified in Proteus.
Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1) with timer-triggered ADC scan conversions and interrupt-driven sample capture.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Built a voice-controlled, vision-guided pick-and-place system over a three-layer distributed pipeline (Flutter client, Flask-SocketIO edge server, Jetson+Arduino controller) linked by a unified WebSocket fabric.

Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture) through system-level debugging across software, communication and hardware; achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end latency.
Integrated TensorRT-optimized YOLO (5.2× speedup, 56.7→10.9 ms) and dual VL53L0X ToF sensors over a TCA9548A I2C mux for contact-aware grasping.
Implemented two-link IK in C++ on Arduino driving five servos; deployed the Jetson bridge as a systemd service (auto-restart, non-root isolation) with static IP networking.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used FreeRTOS mutexes for task coordination on STM32 with interrupt-driven UART commands and multi-servo PWM control, driven by a YOLOv8 tracker on NVIDIA Jetson; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing.
